steps.title: Open the Desk page
steps.narration: We're heading to the Desk page to see the new price disclosure in the ranked briefing table.
steps.point_out: The page loads with a Desk heading and ranked table below the Provenance section.

steps.title: View the ranked table header — now with the new band column
steps.narration: The table header has grown from nine columns to ten. The new 'band' column appears last, after 'history', and shows the exact closing price each row's wall sits at.
steps.point_out: Scroll the table horizontally if needed to see the rightmost 'band' header cell. The full ten-column order is: symbol, side, class, distance, score, coverage, tick evidence, basis, history, band.

steps.title: See the BRK-B row's new band cell
steps.narration: Every ranked row now displays its closing price and band range in the new rightmost cell. On the live store today, all recorded snapshots predate this feature, so this row shows the honest fallback text.
steps.point_out: Find the BRK-B row (leftmost symbol cell). Read its rightmost cell (the new band column) — it shows 'close not recorded in this snapshot'. This is the correct state for legacy snapshots.

expect.text: close not recorded in this snapshot

steps.title: Hover the BRK-B row to see the updated tooltip
steps.narration: The row's composite tooltip has been extended with the new close/band detail, placed right after the existing basis and history information, and before the coverage timestamps.
steps.point_out: Hover over any part of the BRK-B row. The tooltip shows: distance · score · basis · history · 'close not recorded in this snapshot' · coverage windows. The new close detail is positioned between history and the coverage list.

steps.title: Verify pre-existing columns are unchanged
steps.narration: The new band column is purely additive — every other column on the BRK-B row keeps its original value and position. Distance still shows 0.00 bps, score still shows 1787.00, and basis and history information are unchanged.
steps.point_out: Scan across the BRK-B row: side (support), class (Class A), distance (0.00 bps), score (1787.00), coverage (4 timeframe badges lit), basis, and history all render exactly as they did before this iteration.

steps.title: Check another row — LIN shows the same pattern
steps.narration: Scrolling down to find the LIN row confirms the new band column works consistently across all ranked rows. Like BRK-B, it also shows the fallback text because this snapshot predates the feature.
steps.point_out: The LIN row's band cell also reads 'close not recorded in this snapshot'. The distance, score, basis, and history cells match what was recorded before this iteration.

expect.text: close not recorded in this snapshot

steps.title: Confirm the skip table was not affected
steps.narration: The new band column only appears on ranked rows — the skipped members table below deliberately has no band column. This is correct because skipped rows have no distance or band data to disclose.
steps.point_out: Scroll down to the 'Skipped — no bars' section. The skip table has exactly four columns: symbol, reason, coverage, tick evidence. No band column here — this is intentional and working correctly.

steps.title: Summary — the new band disclosure in action
steps.narration: The Desk briefing now surfaces the exact closing price and band range for every ranked row, right where it matters on screen. For snapshots computed after this code ships, operators will see real price numbers. For older snapshots like today's store, the honest fallback message appears instead.
steps.point_out: This purely additive column and tooltip detail move 'price is inside the wall' from unrecoverable arithmetic into a visible, legible fact on every row.
